analysis: The change in ProviderLoop.swift only adds stored state to the ProviderLoop actor: selectedModelRecovery (type SelectedModelRecovery, lines 724-735 on head), selectedModelRecoveryLoadOverride (a test seam, nil in production), savedEnabledModels, and enabledModelsAtLastSwitch. It also adds one initializer line (head line 897) that seeds savedEnabledModels from config.config.backend.enabledModels. The diff contains no new network, crypto, attestation, file or cache-storage code paths. None of these fields touch the wire protocol, key material, attestation (TB-009, TB-011), the prefix cache (T-041), the add-on hold socket (TB-012), or the authorization boundary. savedEnabledModels is read from the operator's own config at init, which is local operator-controlled input already inside the operator trust domain. The new test hook is a closure property that defaults to nil and is internal, not public, so it creates no new production attack surface. The behavior that actually matters is in the companion file ProviderLoop+SelectedModelRecovery (recovery loads that do not evict, the policy refresh that updates savedEnabledModels, and the switch commit that updates enabledModelsAtLastSwitch). It was not supplied, so the next review pass should check whether recovery loads go through the same advertised-set, weight-hash self-test, retiringModels/failedSelfTestHashes, admission-drain and add-on hold gates as ensureModelLoaded. It should also check whether a recovery load could re-serve a model retired for a failed self-test (T-027) or load a model beside an active add-on hold (T-059). Because that code is outside the supplied evidence, I set needs_deeper_review=true and report no findings from this file alone.
